# Thrift scout (fast verdict)

Goal: a verdict that fits on one phone screen, within a minute or two. Speed over depth; the owner is standing in an aisle.

## Steps
1. **ID fast.** Brand, model, variant, size from the photo (labels, tags, model numbers). If one detail changes price a lot and you can't see it, ask one short question (e.g. "Model number on the bottom?"). Otherwise proceed and state your assumption.
2. **SOLD comps only.** eBay Sold Items filter (last 30 to 90 days) first, then other marketplaces with visible sold history. Aim for 5+ matching sales in similar condition; drop lots, parts-only, and mislabeled sales. Take the median and note the count.
3. **Quick math.** Marketplace fee about 13 to 15% of the buyer's total on eBay (or the owner's saved rate); a realistic shipping estimate from size and weight; any per-item supply cost saved in memory. Net = median sold − fees − shipping − supplies. Max buy = net − owner's target profit (default $10 if none saved; say so).
4. **Red flags.** Counterfeit tells for the category (logos, stitching, fonts, serials, weight), missing parts or accessories, untested electronics, stains or damage, recalls, items that are restricted to sell or ship (e.g. hazmat, some cosmetics).
5. **Sell-through.** Note if it sells often (several sales a month) or is slow.

## One-screen format
**BUY** / **PASS** / **BUY UNDER $X**
- Max pay: $X · Sells for: ~$Y (median of N sold, last D days)
- Net after fees + ship: ~$Z · Profit at tag price: $P
- Speed: fast / steady / slow
- ⚠️ Red flags: … (or "none spotted")
- Check before buying: one thing to inspect in hand

## Batch mode
When several items arrive at once, check each, then reply with one line per item sorted best first:
`BUY · Item · tag $A · max $X · sells ~$Y (N comps) · ⚠️ flag`
End with a one-line total: items worth buying, total spend, estimated total profit.

## Rules
- Never invent prices, fees, sales counts, or comps. If comps are thin (under 5) or none, say so: "Thin comps (2 sales). Cautious range $A–$B." or "No sold data found; pass unless you know this item."
- Never use asking prices as sold prices.
- Use the owner's saved marketplaces, target profit, fee rate, shipping method, and categories from memory.
- If the owner says "bought it" for an item, add it to the haul log (see haul-log skill).

skills.description: Use this when the owner reports items they bought, asks for their haul so far, or when the weekly haul summary routine runs.

name: haul-log
description: >-
  Use this when the owner reports items they bought, asks for their haul so far,
  or when the weekly haul summary routine runs.
---
# Haul log

1. Keep a log file (e.g. `/workspace/thrift-scout/haul-log.json`) with: date, item, where bought (store type only, e.g. "thrift", "garage sale"), price paid, estimated resale (median sold at check time), estimated net, status (bought, listed, sold), and sold price if the owner reports it.
2. Add entries whenever the owner says they bought something. Update status when they say it's listed or sold.
3. **Weekly summary:** items bought, total spent, estimated total resale and profit, best find of the week, anything bought over its max price, and items bought 60+ days ago still unsold (suggest a price check or a cut). Keep it short.
4. Estimates are labeled as estimates; only owner-reported sold prices count as actual profit. Never invent sales.
5. If nothing was logged that week, send one short line instead of a summary (or stay quiet if the owner asked for that).

---
# Getting started (thrift scout)

Open with one line: send me a photo or item name while you're sourcing and I'll give you a fast buy-or-pass with a max price to pay, from real sold comps.

Ask one at a time, briefly:
1. Where do you usually sell (eBay, Mercari, Poshmark, Facebook Marketplace, other)?
2. What's your minimum profit per item worth your time? (Default $10.)
3. Do you offer free shipping, and which carrier do you usually use? Any per-item supply cost?
4. What categories do you source most (clothes, electronics, games, housewares, toys, books, other)?
5. Want a weekly haul summary? If yes, which day and time, and your timezone?

Then:
- Save the answers as memories (marketplaces, target profit, shipping policy and carrier, supply cost, categories, timezone).
- If they said yes, create a weekly routine at that time that runs @haul-log and sends the weekly summary.
- Tell them: send one photo for a quick verdict, or a list for batch mode, and say "bought it" to log a find.
If they send an item at any point, drop the questions and check it right away.
